# Express E-commerce API

> Minimal Express + MongoDB e-commerce backend: JWT auth, products, cart,
> checkout, Stripe payments, and shipping. A teaching example of one
> consistent module pattern (route → controller → service → model), not a
> full storefront — expect a narrow feature set.

All business endpoints are versioned under `/api/v1/`. Authenticate by
calling `POST /api/v1/auth/register` or `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, then send
the returned `accessToken` as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on subsequent
requests. Every response is JSON shaped as either `{"success": true, "data":
...}` or `{"success": false, "message": "...", "details"?: ...}` with a
matching HTTP status code.

## Docs

- [OpenAPI document](/openapi.json): Full machine-readable schema (OpenAPI
  3.1) — every endpoint, request/response body, and auth requirement. Read
  this first; it's the source of truth for request/response shapes.
- [Interactive reference](/reference): Human-browsable, try-it-out API
  explorer rendered from the OpenAPI document.
- [Health check](/health): `GET`, returns `{"success":true,"message":"ok"}`
  when the API and its database connection are both up.

## Notes

- Stripe-method checkout is asynchronous: `POST /api/v1/orders` returns an
  order in `pending` status, and `POST /api/v1/payments/checkout-sessions`
  returns a redirect URL — but the order only becomes `paid` once Stripe's
  webhook confirms payment. Poll `GET /api/v1/orders/{id}` rather than
  assuming payment succeeded right after the checkout redirect.
- Cash-on-delivery (`paymentMethod: "cod"`) checkout has no payment gate;
  the order goes straight to `pending` and is confirmed by an admin instead.
- Admin-only endpoints (product/user management, order fulfillment) return
  403 for a `customer`-role token — see the OpenAPI document's per-operation
  `description` for which role each endpoint requires.
